newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAISIO DENIES GENETIC SOYA-BEAN CLAIMS.
newsitem.headline: RAISIO DENIES GENETIC SOYA-BEAN CLAIMS.

text.p: Finnish food, animal feed and chemicals group Raision Tehtaat Oy on Thursday denied allegations by environmental group Greenpeace that it had used oil from genetically modified soya beans in some key margarines.

In a statement, Raisio responded to a press release issued earlier this week by Greenpeace which said some of Raisio's best-known margarine brands like Keiju, Sunnuntai and Benecol might be among those including genetically modified soya bean.
"None of the products include soya bean oil," Raisio said, although it did not deny it had recently received a load of soya beans from the U.S.
The company said it does not favour the use of soya beans, particularly not genetically modified soya beans, as raw material.

"Around two percent of the total U.S. soya bean crop is genetically modified," Raisio said, adding that according to U.S. producers it is impossible to separate the GMO-soya (Gene Modified Organism) from unmodified brands.
The company said it prefers domestic rape seed oil instead of soya bean oil in margarine production.
"The group does not favour soya bean in particular, let alone genetically modified," Raisio said.
